Jolly Helmet User Manual JOLLY HELMET | Make your Helmet Happy Again! Page 32 Circuit and wiring Circuit summary • Every box and refill station is a group of ESP32 boards. They share only power and the radio channel. • Every lock, lamp, pump and heater is switched by a relay contact. Every sensor is read directly by a terminal board. • Voltages: 12 V (door locks, coin slots), 5 V (ESP32 boards, screens, relay boards, HC-SR04 ultrasonic sensors, humidifiers, pumps), 3.3 V (water-level sensors, from the ESP32 3V3 pin or the DC-DC module), 220 V (the UV-C lamps and the heaters). Power and grounding • Measure every output of the DC-DC module (5 V and 3.3 V) with a meter before you connect boards. Never put 12 V on an ESP32 pin or on the 5 V rail. • Join all grounds: 12 V -, 5 V - and every ESP32 GND. Never join a 12 V + to a 5 V +. • A relay module has a JD-VCC jumper. Jumper on: the coils run from the module's VCC (one 5 V supply, shared ground). Jumper off: feed JD-VCC and its GND from a separate 5 V supply. • Locks, pumps and heaters starting can pull the 5 V down. Symptoms: white screen, LocalServer restarts, odd resets. Cures: short thick 5 V wires, a 470 to 1000 μF capacitor next to the TFT and the ESP32, a separate 5 V for the relay coils. The firmware also switches relays on 25 ms apart. • Put a fuse on every supply. Keep the 220 V wiring in its own enclosure, away from the boards.

The neutral goes straight from the supply to the load. The relay board's low- voltage side (IN pins, VCC) stays on the ESP32 side. • Use relay contacts rated for the load. Most relay boards are 10 A at 250 V AC. A hair dryer can draw 8 A or more (read its label). Jolly Helmet User Manual JOLLY HELMET | Make your Helmet Happy Again! Page 48 Safety and emergencies The customer side of every machine is safe to use. The dangers are behind the panels: 220 V mains, UV-C light, a hot heater and flammable alcohol. Read this page before you open anything. In an emergency 1. Stop the run. Touch CANCEL , then CONFIRM . The UV-C, the mist and the heater switch off. Box 2 and Box 3 then cool down for a while (Box 2 runs the fan, Box 3 lets everything rest). The coins are not refunded. 2. A helmet is stuck: see the next block. Never force a door while the machine has power. The locks are power - to - unlock . With the power off, every door stays locked. So after switching off in an emergency, a helmet inside stays inside until power is back. confirm Fit a mechanical key release to each enclosure door if you want a helmet to be freeable without power. A helmet is stuck inside 1. Check that the machine has power. After a power cut, wait until the Control Center Home page shows the boards ONLINE again. 2. Control Center, the box page, Maintenance , tap ENCLOSURE LOCK . The door unlocks for up to 60 seconds, then rests for 5 seconds. Tap Maintenance again when you are done. 3. If the brain of the box stops answering for 15 seconds while a helmet is behind a closed door, the terminal board lets the enclosure lock go by itself. 4. Still locked? Jolly Helmet User Manual JOLLY HELMET | Make your Helmet Happy Again! Page 78 Glossary Words used in this manual, in plain language. Term Meaning ACS Auto Container System. The refill station: pumps and two mixer containers that top up a box's alcohol and scented containers. Allan coin acceptor The coin slot. It sends one pulse for each coin value it accepts. Blynk The online service the Online Server sends its snapshot to. The web page reads it from there. Brain The ESP32 - S3 board of a box (S3A, S3B, S3C). It runs every step and keeps the settings. A box has one brain and several terminals. Captive portal The page that opens by itself when a phone joins the setup Wi - Fi of the Online Server. Channel 1 The radio channel all the boards use for ESP - NOW. The LocalServer Wi - Fi stays on it too. Control Center The pages of the LocalServer (Home, Box 1, Box 2, Box 3, ACS) where settings, calibration and Maintenance are done. Cool down The time after heating when nothing heats and the helmet can cool. Box 2 runs the fan; Box 3 lets everything rest. Datastream A named value in Blynk. This project uses V0 (a text) and, if you switch them on, V1 to V4. DC - DC module The power module that turns 12 V into 5 V and 3.3 V for the boards, sensors and small loads. Enclosure lock The solenoid lock of the main door of a box. It is the one released for a trapped helmet. ESP - NOW The radio link the boards talk over. No router is needed. ESP32 and ESP32 - S3 The two kinds of board. The plain ESP32 boards are terminals. The S3 boards are brains and servers. Free retry One free run after the final rating (2 minutes by default). GPIO A numbered pin of an ESP32 board. Humidifier The ultrasonic mist maker that makes the alcohol and scented mist (5 V). Hysteresis The gap between the WET and the DRY reading of a water sensor, so it does not flicker. JD - VCC The separate power input of a relay module's coils, with a jumper to the logic supply. LocalServer The board that makes the ESP32_LOCAL Wi - Fi and the Control Center, and counts the revenue. Maintenance mode A page where a technician switches relays or pumps by hand. The machine shows MAINTENANCE. Mixer One of the two containers of an ACS (alcohol, scented) where the recipe is made before it goes to a box.

Jolly Helmet User Manual JOLLY HELMET | Make your Helmet Happy Again! Page 79 Term Meaning Mist The alcohol or scented vapour used in cleaning. Mist method: balanced, more alcohol, more scented. NVS The memory inside a board where settings are saved (they survive a power cut). Online Server The ESP32 - S3 that listens to the machines and sends a snapshot to Blynk. It never controls anything. OUT OF ORDER The screen shown when a box cannot serve customers. Phase A part of a cleaning run: start, middle or end. Each relay is on or off per part. Power - to - unlock A lock that opens only while it has power. With no power the door stays locked. Rating The 1 to 10 score the customer gives the helmet before and after: odor (Box 1 and cleaning in Box 3) or dryness (Box 2 and drying). Relay An electrically operated switch. The boards use relays to switch locks, pumps, mist makers, lamps and the heater. SAFETY PAUSE The screen shown when a door opens during a run. The loads switch off until the door is closed. Serial Monitor The Arduino IDE window that shows what a board prints over USB (115200 baud). SoftAP A Wi - Fi network made by a board itself (ESP32_LOCAL, JollyHelmet - Online). Terminal A plain ESP32 board that holds a box's sensors, relays and display. It follows its brain. TFT The 2.8 inch colour touch screen of a box. Time allot The screen where the customer types the minutes to buy. Token The secret key that lets the Online Server write to your Blynk template. Keep it private. Ultrasonic sensor The HC - SR04. It measures the distance to the helmet or to the liquid in a container. UV - C lamp The 220 V germicidal lamp. Never look at it when it is lit. Watchdog A safety check: if a board stops hearing its brain for 15 seconds it switches its loads off.
